Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: And God said to Moses: 'Say to Aaron: stretch forth your hand with your staff over the rivers and the channels and the pools, and bring up the frogs upon the land of Egypt.'
translations.2: And Aaron stretched forth his hand over the waters of the Egyptians, and the frogs came up and covered the land of Egypt.
translations.3: And the learned men did likewise with their secret arts, and brought up frogs upon the land of Egypt.
translations.4: And Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said: 'Intercede with God, that He remove the frogs from me and from my people — and I will release the people, that they may sacrifice to God.'
translations.5: Moses said to him: 'Propose to me: when do you wish that I intercede for you, and for your officers and your people, that the frogs be cut off from you and from your dwellings, and remain in the Nile only?'
translations.6: He said: 'Tomorrow.' He said: 'As you have said it shall be — so that you may know that there is none like God our Lord.'
translations.7: For the frogs shall depart from you and from your dwellings and your officers and your people, and remain in the Nile only.
translations.8: And when Moses and Aaron went out from before Pharaoh, Moses called to God on account of the frogs which He had brought upon Pharaoh.
translations.9: And God did as Moses had said; and the frogs died out of the houses and the courtyards and the villages.
translations.10: And they heaped them up in pile upon pile, and the land stank from them.
translations.11: And when Pharaoh saw that relief had come, he hardened his heart and did not accept from them — as God had said.
translations.12: And God said to Moses: 'Say to Aaron: stretch forth your staff and strike the dust of the earth, that it become lice throughout all the land of Egypt.'
translations.13: And so they did: Aaron stretched forth his hand with his staff and struck the dust of the earth, and the lice came upon the people and the beasts — all the dust of the earth became lice throughout all the land of Egypt.
translations.14: And the learned men did likewise with their secret arts, to bring out the lice, but they could not; and the lice remained upon the people and the beasts.
translations.15: And the learned men said to Pharaoh: 'This is a calamity from God.' But his heart grew firm, and he did not accept from them — as God had said.
translations.16: And God said to Moses: 'Rise early in the morning and stand before Pharaoh — behold, he is going out to the water — and say to him: Thus says God: Release my people, that they may serve Me.'
translations.17: 'For if you refuse to release my people, behold I am sending upon you, and upon your officers, and upon the rest of your people, and upon your dwellings, a mixture of wild beasts — until the houses of the Egyptians shall be filled with it, and the land upon which they dwell.'
translations.18: 'And I shall distinguish on that day the land of Goshen, in which my people dwells, so that no wild beasts shall be there — so that you may know that I am God, sovereign over all the world.'
translations.19: 'And I shall set a ransom for my people from what shall befall your people. Tomorrow shall this sign be.'
translations.20: And God did so; and a great multitude of wild beasts entered the house of Pharaoh and the house of his officers, and all the land of Egypt was ruined because of the wild beasts.
translations.21: And Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron, and said: 'Go, sacrifice to your Lord within the land.'
translations.22: Moses said: 'We cannot do that, for what the Egyptians abhor — that we sacrifice to God our Lord. Shall we then sacrifice what the Egyptians abhor in their very presence, and they not stone us?'
translations.23: 'But a journey of three days we will go into the open country, and sacrifice to God our Lord, as He commands us.'
translations.24: Pharaoh said: 'I will release you, that you may sacrifice to God your Lord in the open country — only do not go far in the journey. Intercede on my behalf.'
translations.25: Moses said: 'Behold, I am going out from before you, and I shall intercede with God, and He shall remove the wild beasts from Pharaoh and his officers and his people tomorrow — only let not Pharaoh repeat the mockery, by not releasing the people to sacrifice to God.'
translations.26: And when he went out from before him, he interceded with God.
translations.27: And God did as Moses had said; and the wild beasts departed from Pharaoh and his officers and his people — not one remained.
translations.28: And Pharaoh hardened his heart this time also, and did not release the people.
